wkplan-2026-07-20.title: Week of July 20–26
wkplan-2026-07-20.review: Week 1 calibration did its job, and you called the miss yourself: two journals flagged that 3 sets on the mains felt like too little volume. You're right — that's a calibration-week artifact (Week 1 of new lifts is deliberately 3 ramping sets to find your numbers), so the 4th work set comes back now that we have them. What you logged: Front Squat 135×5 ('pretty solid'), Incline Bench 145×6 ('significantly stronger'), Push Press 125×6 (you beat the 115 target), Paused DL 225×4 (you noted it needs another week and the knee felt iffy on the last set). So this week: all four mains → 4 work sets; incline bench and push press earn a small top-end nudge (150 / 130); deadlift HOLDS 225 with the 4th set adding only volume, and auto-drops to 205 if the knee complains. Warm-up sets are back on leg press (your ask) and hip thrust. On running — you quietly ran ~17.4 mi, not the 14 the plan asked, and your easy discipline is the best it's been (Sunday's 4-miler came in genuinely easy). So we formalize the progression you're already making: ~18.5 mi, one hard run (Tue, now 6×3 min), the rest strict Z2 — controlled, because the jump from your 12.4-mi deload is already steep and June's burnout is the thing to avoid. Calisthenics gets a real forward step too: push-ups locked at 20 (you moved there on your own), dips to 3 sets, a target to beat on max pull-ups. Big picture on your actual question: the deficit is what's getting you under 190, and it's working — you're ahead of pace. Lifting's job in a cut is to keep the muscle you have (enough volume + heavy loads), not to redline everything at once — that's exactly what re-creates a burnout when you're under-fueled. Next week (7/27) crosses 20 mi and is the last build before the Aug 3 deload.

goals: First: congratulations. Engaged, Red Sox with your brother, a couple days of walking around town — the block just slides, nothing is lost. Tuesday's 4-miler happened, the lift didn't, so the three lifting days now run Wed / Fri / Sat. Saturday calisthenics sits out this week and its one anchor (the max pull-up benchmark) lives inside Saturday's full-body day.

This is the calibration week for the Big-4 retest. Every main lift ramps to ONE top set at ~2 RIR — you log what the bar gives you, and weeks 2–3 build from those numbers toward the Block-1 bests (Squat 200×5, Bench 190, DL 275, OHP ~115 strict). Nothing is a test this week. The listed targets are placeholders from Block 1; if 2 RIR says less, log less without a second thought.

The rebuilt frame protects what matters most: squats today on fresh legs, and Saturday's deadlift calibration with two easy days for the legs in between (Friday is upper only). The cost is Thursday's quality run landing the day after squats — it's threshold, not a race, and there's built-in permission to trim it.

Mileage: Tue 4 (done), Thu 5.5 with the quality work, Fri 1.5 post-lift, Sat 2 post-lift, Sun 2.5 easy — ~17.5 for the week. A touch under the block's ~20 because Monday and Tuesday both went to celebrating; that's the right trade and week 2 sits back at 20.

Strict OHP retests this block (form broke down at 125 back in June — that's why Block 2 ran push press). Friday is strict only: no leg drive, no layback. And the back-care protocol stays on every hinge: extra warm-up, controlled eccentrics, zero grind.

Food: maintenance, full stop. Band is 189–191 and the waist is the arbiter. You're fueling PR attempts for the next three weeks — eat to the SMART goal at deficit 0 and don't react to day-to-day scale noise after a restaurant-heavy celebration stretch.

Saturday update (8/22): a 4th movement (lateral raise + face pull superset) and a 6-set core circuit (hanging leg raise, ab wheel, side plank). That is the new floor for every lift day from here: at least 6 core sets across 2–3 movements, one superset of 2–3 exercises, and core movements rotating through the block's pool instead of repeating.

wkplan-2026-08-17.review: The bridge week did its job: ~13 easy miles, two moderate re-entry lifts, short cabin weekend, sleep re-regulated. Block 2 stays banked — Front Squat 145, Incline 155, Push Press 145, Paused DL 225, pull-up benchmark 18, first 20+ mile week of the rebuild. Then the best possible reason to slide the start: an engagement. Monday and Tuesday went to celebrating (plus a 4-miler), and the barbell work starts today. Three lifting days in the next four set the baselines the whole block progresses from — ramp honestly to 2 RIR, log it, and let weeks 2–3 do the chasing.
